name: DaVita

logo.source: en.wikipedia.org infobox logo (DaVita Inc logo.png, 270x144 PNG, hosted on commons.wikimedia.org)

description: DaVita runs 2,657 outpatient dialysis centers in the US (plus 585 in 14 other countries), treating patients whose kidneys have failed and who need dialysis roughly three times a week for life. It is a payor-mix business: Medicare and Medicare Advantage pay a fixed bundled rate per treatment and cover 57% of US dialysis revenue, but the 11% of patients on non-hospital commercial insurance produce about 26% of US dialysis patient revenue because commercial insurers pay far more per treatment. U.S. dialysis is 86% of revenue and, after a small corporate cost line, essentially all operating income. Growth is in international (revenue up 37.8% in 2025, mostly acquisitions) and in integrated kidney care, where DaVita is paid to manage the health of kidney patients for insurers. Berkshire Hathaway is a large shareholder under a standstill agreement, and DaVita has repurchased a very large share of its stock (14.9% net reduction in shares outstanding in 2025).

businessLines.name: U.S. dialysis and related lab services
businessLines.how: Per-treatment fees: patients typically dialyse three times a week for the rest of their lives, and insurers pay for each treatment. Medicare pays one fixed bundled rate per treatment (57% of revenue from Medicare and Medicare Advantage), commercial insurers pay much higher negotiated rates (32% of revenue incl. hospital dialysis services), and hospitals pay a negotiated per-treatment fee for inpatient dialysis. Revenue is treatments times revenue per treatment, so patient volume and payor mix drive it.
businessLines.description: 2,657 outpatient dialysis centers in 46 states and DC (Dec 31, 2025), home dialysis support, hospital inpatient dialysis under contract with about 740 hospitals, related lab services, and management services to 52 centers it does not fully own.

businessLines.how: Paid by health plans and government programs, in risk-based arrangements where DaVita shares in savings (or losses) on the total cost of care and earns revenue from special needs plans; a physician services business was divested in 2024.
businessLines.description: Care management for health plans and government programs for members with chronic kidney disease or kidney failure; served 66,000 patients in risk-based arrangements and 9,400 in other arrangements at Dec 31, 2025. Part of the 'Other - Ancillary services' reportable segment.

businessLines.name: International dialysis
businessLines.how: Per-treatment fees and administrative-service fees paid by national health systems and insurers in each country; growth has come mostly from buying existing clinics.
businessLines.description: 585 outpatient dialysis centers in 14 countries outside the US serving about 94,500 patients (Dec 31, 2025); net +76 centers in 2025, mainly acquisitions (including Fresenius's Brazil dialysis operations, effective August 1, 2025, for about $94M initial consideration).
